Weight quantization stores model parameters with fewer bits, reducing the memory required to store those parameters, although an aggressive reduction in precision can degrade answer quality. Retrieval-augmented generation supplies relevant course passages when the tutor answers a question. A retrieval encoder maps the question and document passages into embeddings, and a similarity search selects candidate passages from an index. The selected passages are added to the language model's context. Updating this document index can make revised course material available without retraining the language model.
